decision: Which approach best resolves: WF-078 requires a recipient to prove identity before a document opens or before it is signed, and records every attempt in the audit trail. The e-signature workflow (WF-095) cites the same verification object and says identity verification 'is enabled per-workspace (passcode, SMS, KBA, ID check)'. Both specs name the same thing. Exactly one workflow may own the setting so the gate is not implemented twice. Which workflow owns it?

state.problem: WF-078 requires a recipient to prove identity before a document opens or before it is signed, and records every attempt in the audit trail. The e-signature workflow (WF-095) cites the same verification object and says identity verification 'is enabled per-workspace (passcode, SMS, KBA, ID check)'. Both specs name the same thing. Exactly one workflow may own the setting so the gate is not implemented twice. Which workflow owns it?

candidate_solutions.wf078_owns_gate: WF-078 owns the verification settings object on the recipient, the two axes (method as a discriminated union: passcode / phone SMS / KBA / ID; timing as a separate axis: before_open / before_sign), the passcode and E.164 validation, the attempt evaluation, and the withholding of the document body. WF-095 reads the setting and sends the request; it does not enforce it.
candidate_solutions.wf095_owns_gate: WF-095 owns the setting because it owns the document and recipient records the setting lives on. WF-078 becomes a read-only reporter that reads whatever verification_settings it finds and evaluates attempts against them.
candidate_solutions.shared_rule_module: Neither workflow owns it alone. The rule moves into a shared module both import, so the gate has one implementation and neither ticket owns it.
candidate_solutions.wf078_owns_gate_workflow_keyed: WF-078 owns the setting and enforces it, and the setting is keyed per workflow rather than per workspace, so a workspace can require one verification before opening and a different one before signing without the two settings colliding.

context.wf095_note: WF-095 is not implemented in this repository. Nothing imports it, so a design that delegates enforcement to it cannot be tested and cannot be reviewed.

observed_evidence.pandadoc_object: Add verification_settings to a recipient either at document creation or on an existing document. Method table: passcode_verification.passcode 'must be 6-100 characters with at least one letter and one digit'; phone_verification.phone_number 'must be in international format (e.g., +1555667890)'; kba_verification.enabled 'The recipient answers identity questions generated from public records'; id_verification.enabled 'The recipient verifies identity with a government-issued ID'. Timing: before_open = 'Before the recipient can view the document' / 'All recipients'; before_sign = 'Before the recipient can sign' / 'Signers only'.
observed_evidence.audit_codes: 47 recipient verification with kba passed; 51 recipient verification with kba failed; 69 recipient verification with email otp passed; 70 recipient verification with email otp failed. Codes 47-54 are the verification band.
observed_evidence.automation: Verification is re-asserted by the gate on every attempt; there is no 'verify once, remember forever' behaviour. Both success and failure produce audit actions, so a rejected attempt is as visible as a successful one.
observed_evidence.data_flow: Verification config is persisted on the recipient record. At the chosen gate the recipient's identity is proven out of band and the result is stamped onto the recipient's session; the document body is withheld until it clears.
observed_evidence.already_in_this_repository: dsr/audit_export/vocabulary.py already owns the integer action-code vocabulary and already lays out codes 47-50 as four pass codes and 51-54 as four fail codes, with the method order (kba, passcode, sms, id). It is the only place a verification code is defined, and it is WF-079's.

requirements: The feature adds files and edits no shared file.
Every write goes through AuditedDatabase so the audit row lands in the same transaction.
Records are ordinary JSON in records.data. No migration and no typed column.
The setting, the two axes, the passcode bound, the E.164 bound and the attempt audit must all be enforceable and testable in this repository on its own.
A team adding a field must need no coordination with anyone.
constraints: The four domain packages available to extend are crm_integration, throttle, lead_score, visitor_identification, lead_qualification, round_robin and concierge_router. dsr/security_governance exists and is WF-073's.
A feature may not import another feature module.
The integer code vocabulary belongs to dsr.audit_export.vocabulary and must not be minted a second time.

state.change_summary:
WF-078 requires a recipient to prove identity before a document opens or before it is
signed, and records every attempt in the audit trail.

WHAT WAS BUILT

A domain package backend/dsr/identity_verification with four modules: vocabulary (the
researched terms), rules (the two independent axes, the passcode and E.164 bounds, the
attempt evaluation, the four error types), inferences (every judgement call with the
alternative it rejected), and engine (the writes). Plus a feature module
backend/dsr/features/wf078_require_recipient_identity_verification.py exporting FEATURE
and a router on prefix /api/wf-078 with 20 routes, plus backend/tests/test_wf078.py and
backend/tests/test_wf078_http.py, plus
frontend/src/features/wf-078-require-recipient-identity-verification/ with index.jsx,
api.js, primitives.jsx, icons.js, fixtures.js and 53 tests.

THE DESIGN

The method is a discriminated union on the recipient and the timing is a separate axis, so
verification_settings is a mapping keyed by gate. That is the shape the specification's
extensibility note requires: "the same recipient object can be verified differently for
viewing and signing". One method and one moment per recipient cannot express it. The
audience difference is sourced rather than chosen: the timing table gives before_open
"All recipients" and before_sign "Signers only", so a non-signer is refused a before_sign
gate and one that somehow holds it fails the attempt rather than passing it.

An attempt records the facts of what happened and takes the integer action code through a
code_for callable the caller supplies. The feature module passes
dsr.audit_export.vocabulary.verification_code, which already owns the 47 to 54 band over
the same four methods. Two tables describing the same integers would drift the first time a
team reordered a method, so the code table has one home and this workflow has no import edge
to it.

WHY NOT THE ALTERNATIVES

The e-signature workflow and this one both describe the same verification object. Jev was
asked which owns it, chose this workflow owning the gate over delegating enforcement, a
shared rule module and workflow-keyed settings, at confidence 0.93, audit
jev-20261004T140557-22596-57651. Delegating enforcement was rejected on evidence: WF-095 is
not implemented in this repository, so a design that hands it the gate cannot be tested and
cannot be reviewed.

Holding secrets in clear was rejected. A passcode and a one-time code are compared with
secrets.compare_digest, a passcode is never returned from a recipient projection or a
prompt, and a code is never returned by the send that issued it. A send endpoint that handed
the code back would have turned the gate into a suggestion.

Remembering a pass was rejected. The specification says verification "is re-asserted by the
gate on every attempt; there is no verify once, remember forever behaviour", so the gate is
resolved from the LATEST attempt and a later failure withholds the body again. A test proves
it: pass, body released, fail, body withheld again.

WHAT COULD NOT BE DONE

Nothing was skipped. Every acceptance criterion in issue 172 was exercised. The only limits
are measurement limits and they are listed in declared_unverified below.

measurements.own_backend_files: tests/test_wf078.py and tests/test_wf078_http.py, 197 tests, run alone, 197 passed
measurements.whole_backend_suite: 15058 passed, 1 xfailed, 0 failed, exit code 0, measured under pytest-xdist with four agents running on the same machine
measurements.seed_ran: backend/seed.py printed the WF-078 line with states that are not all successes: 4 verified documents, 5 recipients (4 gated, 1 ungated), 1 carrying both moments at once, 3 attempts, 2 passed and 1 failed
measurements.ruff_check: All checks passed, from the repository root with --config backend/pyproject.toml
measurements.frontend_lint: 0 errors; the 12 remaining warnings are in other agents' pre-existing files
measurements.frontend_format_check: not run separately; npm run format:check is a whole-tree prettier check
measurements.contract_guard: python tools/check_feature_diff.py --base origin/main reported OK: 15 changed file(s), none shared
measurements.design_floor: python tools/check_design_floor.py --feature wf-078-... reported 0 failing, 0 with warnings
measurements.diff_after_rebase: git diff --stat origin/main..HEAD showed 15 files changed, 8346 insertions, 0 deletions

declared_unverified: No screen reader was run. The ARIA roles and labels are asserted from source and the accessible names are asserted through jsdom queries, but no assistive technology was driven.
No browser was driven. The page is proven by 53 jsdom tests against recorded API fixtures and by a successful production build; the design-floor checker reads source patterns rather than a render.

Contrast ratios were not measured. The page uses semantic tokens only and no raw hex, and docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md states that foreground and muted-foreground pass 4.5:1 on background and surface, but no computed style was read from a render.
Responsive behaviour was not checked at 375, 768, 1024 or 1440 pixels. The layout uses the documented grid and collapse classes, which the checker does not read.

No SMS was actually sent. The gate is proven end to end because this room generates and holds the code, which DERIVED_SMS_CODE_IS_THE_ROOM'S records as a decision: no gateway is named in any cited source.

The whole-suite numbers were measured on a machine running four agents at once, so the wall-clock figure understates what a clean runner would show. The pass and fail counts are not affected by contention.
npm run format:check was not run for this feature. It is a whole-tree prettier check whose result would describe other agents' files, not this branch.
state.requirements: A feature adds files and edits no shared file. All reads and writes go through dsr.deps / RecordStore / AuditedDatabase so every mutation writes its audit row in the same transaction. Payloads stay schema-flexible JSON: no migration, no typed column, the envelope untouched. The feature owns a unique route prefix with no colliding concrete (method, path) pair. Tests exist and the whole suite is green. The frontend page builds, is discovered by the glob, and meets the design floor.

contract_compliance.instructions: Does this change add only new files and leave every shared file untouched, per the feature contract?

criteria.true: No shared file is edited, and the contract guard confirms it on a non-empty diff
criteria.false: A shared file is edited, or the guard did not actually measure a diff

claims_backed_by_measurement.instructions: Is every claim made in the evidence supported by a measurement that was actually run, rather than asserted, read off a progress bar, or produced by a check that passed on empty input? Declared limits are not a failure of this question -- they are the honest disclosure that belongs to them.

criteria.true: Each claim traces to quoted, reproducible tool output
criteria.false: A claim is asserted, or a check passed vacuously or was not run

coverage_of_the_change.instructions: Setting aside what is declared unverified, how much of the change did the evidence actually exercise? Judge breadth, not honesty: a declared limit is fine, but a large unexamined surface is not.

criteria.true: Every surface the change introduces is exercised by a measurement, with at most incidental limits declared
criteria.false: A substantial part of the change was never measured, whether or not that is declared

audit_integrity.instructions: Does this change preserve the audited-store guarantee: all writes through the wrapper, no direct database connection, no schema change outside the envelope?

criteria.true: Writes go through the audited store and the envelope is unchanged
criteria.false: A direct connection is opened, or a typed column or migration is added

design_floor.instructions: Does the frontend meet the design floor -- 44px touch targets, visible focus, a text label beside every icon, no emoji as icons, reduced motion respected -- as checked by the scripted pass?

criteria.true: The scripted design-floor pass is green
criteria.false: The pass is red, was skipped, or is on the allowlist

verdict.instructions: Should this change land on main? Weigh the balance of the questions above rather than deciding on your own: where contract_compliance, audit_integrity and design_floor are all healthy and the evidence questions show broad coverage, answer merge with the confidence that warrants. Items listed as unverified are declared context to weigh, not defects in themselves -- but a change whose coverage is genuinely thin, or which was recovered from a base far behind main and not reconciled, is fix.

criteria.merge: Evidence supports landing it: suite green, contract intact, floor met
criteria.fix: Worth keeping but needs work against current main before landing
